The petitioner has filed this writ petition seeking following reliefs:-
"10.1

The Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to issue the appropriate writ / orders by quasing the proclamation notice for sale issued by respondent No. 2 and 4 dated 05.04.2023 and 24.08.2023.
10.2

The Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to issue the appropriate writ/orders directing the respondents authorities to issue allotment orders in favour of the petitioner for the land situated at Debabrata Shil vs The State Of Chhattisgarh on 8 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84396791/

10.3

Any other relief which this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice and cost of the petition may be awarded in favour of the petitioner."

2. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that pursuant to policy of State Government dated 11.09.2019 for settlement of encroached Government land and allotment of Government land,
petitioner submitted an application for allotment of land bearing khasra No. 951/1 measuring 400 square meters situated at Pakhanjore Distt. - North Bastar, Kanker (C.G.).
The Tahsildar processed the application of petitioner, called report from the Revenue Inspector, who, in turn, submitted report on 27.06.2020.
Based on the report submitted by Revenue Inspector, panchnama was also prepared in this regard.
Copy of the report of Revenue Inspector and panchnama are placed in record.

After receipt of report, a District level Committee consisting Chief Municipal Officer,
Assistant Director, Nagar tatha Gram Nivesh, Additional Collector cum President, District Level Commitee constituted under the policy dated 11.09.2019, examined the claim / application of petitioner, recommended for allotment of said land to the petitioner on his depositing premium amount of Rs. 13,91,032/- and forwarded the same to the Collector, who is the competent authority under the Policy of State Government for taking decision for allotment of Government Land.

It is submission of learned counsel for petitioner that based on the report of the Committee, the Tahsildar issued demand note of Rs. 13,91,032/- as per requirement of policy, which petitioner has deposited in the Treasury on 30.06.2020, copy of chalan is also enclosed along with this writ petition.

When no order on the application submitted by petitioner for allotment of land was passed by the competent authority, petitioner filed writ petition before this Court bearing W.P.(C.) No.
1086 of 2022 which was disposed of vide order dated 28.02.2022 with a direction to the concerned authority to take appropriate decision on the issue of allotment of Government land to the petitioner.

In compliance of the said direction, and the new policy of the State Government dated 24.02.2022, decision was taken on 05.04.2023 by the Committee observing that the land can be allotted only by way of an auction.

Learned counsel for petitioner submits that the claim of petitioner was processed pursuant to earlier policy dated 11.09.2019 and therefore, claim of petitioner ought to have been finalized considering the clauses under earlier policy as subsequent policy after processing claim of petitioner for allotment of Government land is not applicable.

He submits that when the petitioner has already deposited substantial amount against the demand note, petitioner cannot be put to disadvantageous position and action of respondent State in dismissing claim of petitioner for allotment in midst of the proceedings is per se arbitrary and illegal.
3. Learned State counsel opposing the submissions made by learned counsel for the petitioner,
would submit that during pendency of the claim of petitioner for allotment of the Government land,
subject matter of writ petition, the State Government has withdrawn its policy dated 11.09.2019 and has introduced new policy dated 24.02.2022 for allotment of Government land.

In the said policy,
allotment of Government land is to be made only by way of auction.
He submits that said decision is taken only to protect loss to State ex-chequer.

In the earlier policy, under which petitioner has Debabrata Shil vs The State Of Chhattisgarh on 8 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84396791/
2 submitted an application, it is the Collector who is competent authority to pass an order of allotment of land to any applicant, said application and the proceedings was not placed before the Collector.
Till taking a decision by the respondent authority pursuant to the new policy dated 24.02.2022, no right has been accrued in favour of petitioner as the application of petitioner was not finalized at any point of time.

sentences.text: 4. I have heard learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the documents annexed along with this writ petition.
5. Petitioner has placed on record the policy formulated by the State Government for allotment and settlement of Government land in favour of person who has encroached upon it.
Under Clause 2 of the said policy, the Collector has been mentioned to be Competent Authority for allotment of the Government land and its settlement as per the claim.

It is not in dispute that in response to earlier policy on 12.03.2020, petitioner submitted an application before the Tahsildar for allotment of Government land bearing khasra no. 951/1 measuring 400 square meter situated in Pakhanjur,
Distt. - North Bastar, Kanker (C.G.) supported with an affidavit.
On receipt of application, Tahsildar has called for the report from the Revenue Inspector, who, in turn, submitted report on 26.06.2020.
In the said report, there is specific mention that petitioner is not in possession of the land applied for and the land is lying vacant.

After receipt of the report, application was further forwarded to the Committee constituted under the policy of the State Government dated 11.09.2019 for considering the application and entitlement of petitioner for allotment.

The District Level Committee constituted for allotment of land / settlement of Government land considered the application,
forwarded its decision in which the Committee has assessed and calculated the amount of premium to be paid by petitioner for allotment of Government land applied for i.e.Rs. 13,91,032/-.
It is further mentioned that upon applicant depositing aforementioned amount, the proceedings shall be forwarded to the Collector.
It is the claim of petitioner that thereafter the Tahsildar has raised a demand for deposit of said amount and accordingly, petitioner deposited Rs. 13,91,032 /- through bank chalan.

6. It is not the case of any of the parties that the demand is raised by the competent authority after finalizing the claim of petitioner holding him to be entitled for allotment of Government land applied for.
It is the Tahsildar who raised the demand, but Tahsildar is not the competent authority to consider the claim of applicant as per the policy formulated by the State Government in the year 2019.

No document has been placed in record to show that the Tahsildar or the Committee constituted under the policy has forwarded the claim / proceedings of petitioner to the Collector,
who is the competent authority for allotment of the land.
Meaning thereby, the proceedings based on the application submitted by petitioner was still at the initial stage.

Before the proceedings initiated by Tahsildar on the application submitted by petitioner, could reach to the office of Collector, i.e. the competent authority, the State Government has withdrawn its earlier policy and brought in force new policy for allotment of the land on 24.02.2022, in which, the provision for allotment of land is only through auction proceedings.
Definitely, in the auction proceedings, the State Government may get higher rates and land is to be allotted to the person who would submitted highest bid.
If, this writ petition is allowed, it may cause revenue loss to the State ex-chequer.

The decision rendered in case of Yashdeep Singh Saini v. Naya Raipur Development Authority,
Chhattisgarh, ILR 2020 Chhattisgarh 869, which is relied upon by the learned counsel for petitioner, is distinguishable on facts.

entities.text:
Yashdeep Singh Saini v. Naya Raipur Development Authority,
Chhattisgarh, ILR 2020 Chhattisgarh 869
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, respondents therein had purchased the land of petitioner therein under the mutual purchase scheme, say of petitioner therein was that the land was sold on the nominal rates because respondents therein had promised to allot two plots in the developed area i.e. Naya Raipur, but later on, they did not keep their promise.

Under such circumstances, this Court has observed that the acquisition was not as like of general contract of sale and purchase on free will of the parties or was acquired under the Right To Fair Compensation And Transparency In Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and held that in the facts of the case, respondents would be arrested on the principle of primary estoppel.

entities.text: Right To Fair Compensation And Transparency In Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 8. In the case at hand, the application submitted by petitioner for allotment of Government land was processed, however, competent authority has not taken final decision.

The application was not processed before the competent authority who, as per the policy, has to collect all the materials like report of Revenue Inspector, calculation of the amount of premium, which is required to be paid,
and ultimate decision for allotment, based on the application was to be taken by the Collector.
Admittedly, in case at hand, the file has not been reached to the office of Collector and he has not applied his mind, to the facts of the case.

When the State Government has changed the policy for allotment of Government land, petitioner would not be entitled to seek a writ of mandamus directing the State Government to allot the land based on its earlier policy which was withdrawn by the State Government.
9. For the foregoing discussion and reasons, I do not find any merit in this writ petition.
Accordingly, it is dismissed.

However, as petitioner has deposited the amount in the year 2020,
pursuant to demand note raised by the Tahsildar in a proceedings on the application submitted by petitioner, therefore, respondent State authorities are directed to refund the amount deposited by petitioner along with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date on which it is deposited till its realization,
within a period of eight weeks from the date of production of the order.
